description: The mathematics that computer science is written in: logic, proof, sets, relations, counting, number theory and graphs, taught by proving and computing rather than memorising. Taught to the depth of the standard mathematics-for-computer-science course, with every proof technique practised on real problems.
modelledOn: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
Lehman, Leighton and Meyer, Mathematics for Computer Science
outcomes: Translate English statements into propositional and predicate logic and check validity with truth tables and inference rules.
Write correct proofs by direct argument, contrapositive, contradiction, cases and induction, including strong and structural induction.
Work fluently with sets, functions and relations, and prove properties such as injectivity, equivalence and partial order.
Count arrangements with permutations, combinations, the pigeonhole principle and inclusion-exclusion, and solve recurrences.
Apply modular arithmetic, GCD and the Chinese remainder theorem, including to RSA.
Model problems as graphs and reason about paths, trees, colourings and planarity.

units.title: Propositional and predicate logic
topics: Propositions, connectives, truth tables, tautologies and contradictions
Logical equivalence, De Morgan's laws, conditional and biconditional, converse and contrapositive
Rules of inference: modus ponens, modus tollens, resolution; valid and invalid arguments
Predicates and quantifiers; nested quantifiers; negating quantified statements
Normal forms (CNF, DNF) and satisfiability; logic puzzles

units.title: Proof techniques
topics: Axioms, definitions, theorems, lemmas; what a proof is and is not
Direct proof, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction, proof by cases
Existence and uniqueness proofs; counterexamples
Common errors: circular reasoning, proving the converse, division by zero
Proof that the square root of 2 is irrational; infinitude of primes

units.title: Sets, functions and relations
topics: Set notation, subsets, power sets, Cartesian products; set operations and identities; Venn diagrams
Binary operations on sets; closure, associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse
Functions: domain, codomain, image; injective, surjective, bijective; composition and inverse
Relations: reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive; equivalence relations and partitions
Partial orders, Hasse diagrams, lattices; closures of relations
Cardinality: countable and uncountable sets, Cantor's diagonal argument

units.title: Number systems and number theory
topics: Integers, rationals, reals; positional number systems and base conversion
Divisibility, primes, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
The division algorithm, Euclid's algorithm, extended Euclid and Bezout's identity
Modular arithmetic, congruences, inverses mod n; Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem
Chinese remainder theorem; RSA encryption as an application
Representing integers and floating-point numbers in a computer

units.title: Sequences, series, induction and recursion
topics: Sequences and summation notation; arithmetic and geometric series; telescoping sums
Weak and strong induction; well-ordering principle; common induction mistakes
Recursive definitions of sequences, sets and functions; structural induction
Solving linear recurrences: characteristic equations, Fibonacci closed form
Recursive algorithms and proving them correct; towers of Hanoi, merge sort recurrence
Asymptotic notation: big-O, big-Omega, big-Theta

units.title: Counting and combinatorics
topics: Sum and product rules; permutations and combinations; binomial theorem and Pascal's triangle
Pigeonhole principle and its generalisation
Inclusion-exclusion; derangements
Counting with repetition; stars and bars; distributing objects into boxes
Introduction to discrete probability: sample spaces, events, conditional probability

units.title: Boolean algebra
topics: Boolean algebra as a mathematical structure; axioms and duality
Boolean functions, truth tables, sum-of-products and product-of-sums expressions
Simplification with identities and Karnaugh maps
Logic gates and circuits as Boolean expressions; functional completeness of NAND
Boolean algebra and set algebra as the same lattice

units.title: Graph theory
topics: Graphs, digraphs, multigraphs; degree, handshaking lemma; adjacency matrix and list
Paths, cycles, connectivity, components; Euler circuits and Hamiltonian cycles
Trees, spanning trees, rooted trees; properties and counting of trees
Shortest paths with Dijkstra; minimum spanning trees with Kruskal and Prim
Graph colouring, chromatic number, bipartite graphs and matching
Planar graphs and Euler's formula; modelling road networks and timetables as graphs
